AGENDA
  ALHAMBRA YOUTH COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  Alhambra Public Library, Learning Center - 101 S. First Street, Alhambra, CA
  91801 Tuesday, August 8, 2023 - 6:00 PM

Commissioners  Members Ex Officio
Daniela Andrade  Michael Macias, Director of Parks & Recreation
Joselyn Cooper  Brie Houghton, Deputy Director
Marilyn Gonzalez  Rosalyn Rojas, Recreation Supervisor
Tatiana Hernandez
Iren Lam
Zachary Oliva
Jason Quach
Natalia Rosales
Andy Tiang
Chen Yu

We welcome you to the Youth Commission meeting.
If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and
give it to the secretary. The maximum time for addressing the Commission is five minutes. If
you wish to address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments
will be heard during the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the
Commission on a subject which does not appear on the agenda but related to recreation or
community service, you may make your presentation under agenda item VII. Please be advised
that the Commission cannot, under the State of California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, take action on
any item which does not appear on the agenda.
When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please make
your statement as brief as possible. Thank you.

I.  Roll Call
II.  Flag Salute
III.  Approval of the Minutes of the regular meeting of July 11, 2023. Recommended
Action: Approve the minutes of July 11, 2023. *Note: you must have attended the meeting
to vote on the minutes.
 IV.  Staff Report
V.  Oral Communications
VI.  Commission Orals
VII.  Adjournment
Copies of staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described
hereinabove are on file in the Department of Parks & Recreation, Alhambra City Hall, 111 South
First Street, Alhambra, California, and are available for public inspection during regular office
hours which are 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday.
Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the
meeting described herein, he or she may contact Mr. Michael Macias, Director of Parks &
Recreation, either in person at the Department of Parks & Recreation or by telephone at
626-570-5044.
minutes_text:
Minutes
  Alhambra Youth
  Commission August 8, 2023

The Alhambra Youth Commission was called to order at 6:11 PM on August 8, 2023 at the
Alhambra Civic Center Library, 101 S. 1st St. Alhambra, CA 91801

Commission Members Present: T. Hernandez, I. Lam, M. Gonzalez, N. Rosales and J. Quach

Commission Members Absent: D. Andrade, J. Cooper, Z. Oliva, A. Tiang and C. Yu

Also present: Deputy Director - B. Houghton, Supervisor - R. Rojas and Program Coordinator - F. Reyes

Flag Salute

Approval of Minutes
Commissioner M. Gonzalez motioned to approve the Minutes of July 6, 2023 meeting. T. Hernandez
second the motion. Youth Commission President J. Quach recommened proof reading the mintues due
to a typo on page 2 of random letters.

Staff Report
Deputy Director B. Houghton thanked the Commissioners for volunteering at the Movies in
the Park event. Supervisor R. Rojas referred the list of remaining 2023 City events she emailed
to the Youth Commision President for volunteering opportunities. Supervisor Rojas stated she
would forward the list to the Commissioners. She also mentioned the park murals as an
opportunity for volunteering. She suggested they review the list and let City Staff know which
events they were intrested in.

Oral Communications
No cards submitted for oral comminications.

Commission Orals
President J. Quach recommended the Youth Commission "opt-out" of the Tech Talk program
because it's not "youth" based. Deputy Director Houghton informed the Commission it was
recommended they be a part of Tech Talk by the City Council as part of the City's Strategic Plan.
In efforts to bridge the gap between the City's youth and seniors. Deputy Houghton stated she
could take the request to the City Council for the Commission to be removed as part of Tech
Talk. Commissioner T. Hernandez suggested since schools are back in session, the Service
Groups needing service hours could volunteer at Tech Talk. Deputy Houghton proposed the
Commissioners each choose a month for Tech Talk to share the responsibility, giving them a
month to gather volunteers. Deputy Houghton suggested a spreadsheet with the remaining Tech
Talk dates so the Commissioners can choose the month they would participate in and organize
volunteers.

President J. Quach inquired about clarification on the Brwon Act and how they can
communicate by email, text, or chat. Deputy Houghton clarified texts and chatting are okay, the
in-person group meetings of more than five, a quorum, is what they need to be mindful of. She
stated she's open to the various types of communication with the Commissioners as long as she
can get them to respond.

President J. Quach wanted to addess a miscommunication about the role of the Commission for
the Movies in the Park event. He understood they'd be tabling at the event.
 Deputy Houghton and Supervisor Rojas clarified the Commission's role was to assist and
support City Staff with the event where needed. The Youth Commission has not yet confirmed
any future projects, volunteer opportunities, or flyers for distribution for a tabling.

President J. Quach asked if the Commission could meet more often and made reference to Ad
Hoc meetings. Deputy Houghton said they could meet as long as they have a specific project
they're working on. She mentioned working on their flyer layout, planning for future events
they want to volunteer at, etc.

President J. Quach asked the Commission what they wanted to focus on for the remainder of
the year. He mentioned donations for a back-to-school drive or other ideas. Supervisor Rojas
mentioned she'd send a sample donation letter, the Tech Talk dates, and the City events to the
Commissioners. Deputy Houghton suggested a toy drive or a book drive. Giving them more
time to plan. President J. Quach recommended a food drive. Commissioner I. Lam shared that
her service club volunteers for a monthly food drive, and she can get the Youth Commission to
be a part of it if interested. Supervisor Rojas suggested the Commission take it to a vote to
volunteer at a food drive and lead their project like a toy drive. Deputy Houghton echoed her
thoughts. Deputy Houghton asked if there's a local children's shelter the Commission could
donate the toys to. Coordinator Reyes suggested they come up with a plan of action of what
they want to attack, decide what they're passionate about, and revisit the strategic plan. To
think about what charitable organizations they want to benefit. Deputy Houghton shared how
they're building a chair volleyball team and how they can host a tournament with the Youth
Commission. Commissioner I. Lam suggested the Volleyball tournament to help build the
Commission's name to help with future events such as toy drives. Commissioner T. Hernandez
said the girl's volleyball season just started, and they could help with the chair volleyball.
President J. Quach said the same about the boy's volleyball team. Commissioner N. Rosales
said that once this volleyball team's created they can add an athletic clothing drive for seniors.

President J. Quach made a motion for them to do a toy drive. It passed unanimously. Deputy
Houghton confirmed they're focusing on a toy drive with the Spark of Love. They can start
working on the donation letter and include the service groups. Coordinator Reyes suggested
they select dates for the Famers Market to collect toy donations.

President J. Quach asked if the Youth Commission could have their own Instagram. Deputy
Houghton explained how they could not at this time and how the City could promote and post
on social media on their behalf.

Deputy Houghton and the commissioners suggested the various toy drop box locations. She
suggested they start working on the flyer for verbiage. Supervisor Rojas said they should use
an approved template or flyer when promoting.

Commissioner M. Gonzalez said they can promote the flyer in the Moor Weekly.
Commissioner T. Hernandez said they could promote the flyer on the ASB Instagram page.
Deputy Houghton said, they can also do reposting because they get a lot of traction.
Commissioner T. Hernandez are part of the PTA said they can help promote the toy drive.

Commissioner N. Rosales said she could promote at her school La Canada Flitridge. Supervisor
Rojas suggested they hold an Ad Hoc meeting before the next Youth Commission meeting to
work on a draft flyer for the toy drive.
 Deputy Houghton asked the Commission to resubmit their contact information, email, and cell
phone number to ensure we are in contact.

Adjournment
President J. Quach motioned for adjournment at approximately 7:19 PM. Seconded by
Commissioner I. Lam.
